channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Afghanistan's Core Problem: Structural Underdevelopment, Not Political System
item.description: Afghanistan faces numerous crises, with debate centering on political systems. However, the core issue is structural underdevelopment, not the political system itself. While Western models are often cited, solutions must consider Afghanistan's unique historical, social, economic, and cultural conditions. Changing the political system alone may not resolve the country's deep-seated problems.

item.title: Former Head Doctor of Aktobe Clinic Sentenced for Embezzling 53 Million Tenge
item.description: The former head doctor of Clinic No. 3 in Aktobe, Zhanibek Narmukhametov, has been sentenced to five years of probation for fraud. State media reported that he embezzled over 53 million tenge from the Social Health Insurance Fund by submitting false data on medical services provided. He confessed and repaid the damages.

item.title: Kazakhstan Issues Storm Warning: Freezing Temperatures and Snow Expected in 17 Regions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kazhydromet has issued a storm warning for Astana and 17 regions on October 18. Forecasters predict freezing temperatures down to -7 degrees Celsius, with snow, ice, fog, and dust storms expected. Some areas, like Zhetysu and Almaty regions, will experience significant frost, while others face strong winds and fog.

item.title: Protests in France Turn Violent, Over 100 Arrested in Paris and Other Cities
item.description: Protests across several French cities on October 17 escalated into clashes, with over 100 arrests reported in Paris. Police used tear gas and water cannons in the capital. In Marseille, protesters stormed a municipal police station and damaged the building. Road blockades were attempted in Lyon, Rennes, and other cities.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Health Ministry to Inspect Almaty Clinic Over Alleged Fake Medical Certificates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is initiating an unscheduled inspection of the private clinic "Ayazhan" in Almaty. This follows social media reports alleging the issuance of fake medical certificates and health books. The ministry reminds citizens of criminal liability for forging or using fraudulent documents, emphasizing that medical documents must reflect actual examinations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China Plan to Increase Direct Flights Between Cities
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with a delegation led by Chinese Premier Li Qiang to discuss strengthening strategic partnerships. Discussions included implementing agreements from previous high-level meetings. Both nations reaffirmed cooperation on counter-terrorism, separatism, and extremism. Plans are underway to increase direct flights, boost trade, and expand cooperation in green energy and other sectors.

item.title: Astana's Old Train Station Inspected for Accessibility Before Reopening
item.description: Experts inspected Astana's reconstructed "Astana-1" railway station for accessibility for people with limited mobility before its launch. Recommendations were provided. The inspection covered approaches, entrances, internal routes, restrooms, and platforms. Kazakhstan's new Construction Code, effective July 1, 2026, mandates accessibility compliance for people with disabilities and other mobile-impaired groups.

item.title: Gold and Silver Prices Increase on Global Markets
item.description: The price of gold rose by $11 per troy ounce to $4,181.1 on the COMEX commodity exchange in New York. Silver prices also increased by $0.15 to $57.31 per troy ounce. This follows a period of decline, with gold losing approximately 5% in the last month and its annual growth narrowing to 2.5%.

item.title: Prisoner dies in Kazakhstan days before release, authorities investigate
item.description: A prisoner at the №1 institution in the penal system in Atbasar city, Akmola region, died shortly before his scheduled release. The Department of the Criminal-Executive System for the Akmola region confirmed the death, stating it was a suicide. No external injuries were found on the body. The incident is under investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes preventive diplomacy mechanism at CICA summit in Baku
item.description: At the CICA summit in Baku, Kazakhstan proposed a mechanism for preventive diplomacy to address disputes before they escalate. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated the mechanism would involve all member states in decision-making. Kazakhstan also coordinates CICA’s military-political dimension and influenced the establishment of the Think Tank Forum.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Released from South Korean Prison After 16 Years on Life Sentence
item.description: A 37-year-old Uzbek national, Akmal Bozorov, was released from a South Korean prison on October 15 after serving over 16 years of a life sentence for robbery and murder. His retrial was granted after new evidence emerged regarding police protocol falsification and rights violations, including the absence of a translator during interrogations. Bozorov expressed remorse for the victim's family.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China May Increase Air Travel Between Cities, President Meets Chinese Premier
item.description: Air travel between cities in Uzbekistan and China could be increased, following a meeting between the Uzbek President and the Chinese Premier. The meeting emphasized expanding exchanges in tourism, culture, and education. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Afghan Red Crescent Discusses Humanitarian Cooperation with Austrian and Danish Counterparts
item.description: The Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) met with representatives from the Austrian and Danish Red Cross to discuss expanding humanitarian cooperation. Discussions focused on aid for vulnerable families and support for returning refugees. ARCS President thanked the organizations for their ongoing assistance, particularly after the Kunar earthquake.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Grain, Meat, and Vegetable Oil Exports to Cambodia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov met with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet in Astana to discuss trade and economic cooperation. Bektenov expressed interest in supplying Kazakh grain, vegetable oils, and meat to Cambodia. They also explored joint agricultural projects, irrigation technologies, and developing transport routes, including connecting the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route with Southeast Asian corridors.

item.title: Kazakhstan and EU Discuss Trans-Caspian Route Development and Investment Attraction
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issetov and EU Special Representative for Central Asia Edvards Stiprais held talks in Astana. They discussed the development of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, attracting European investments, and implementing infrastructure projects. Cooperation within the 'Central Asia - European Union' format was also a key topic.

item.title: Pakistan Links Taliban Talks to Action Against Militants Operating from Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan's Foreign Ministry stated that any dialogue with the Taliban hinges on concrete, verifiable action against armed groups operating from Afghanistan. Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan emphasized that talks must yield tangible security results. Pakistan also noted its contacts with Russia regarding Afghanistan but was unaware of a formal Russian mediation initiative.

item.title: Migrant Raid Conducted Near Sennoy Market in St. Petersburg; Dozens Detained
item.description: A raid targeting migrants was conducted near the Sennoy Market in St. Petersburg, with law enforcement detaining dozens of individuals. Their documents were checked, and their military registration status was verified, particularly for those recently granted Russian citizenship. Further details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry of Health to Inspect Private Clinic Over Suspected Sale of Fake Medical Certificates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is initiating an unscheduled inspection of the "Ayazhan" private clinic in Almaty following social media reports of alleged fake medical certificates and personal health books being issued. The ministry stated that if violations are confirmed, appropriate measures will be taken. Criminal liability exists for document forgery and fraudulent use.

item.title: Worker in Coma After 5-Meter Fall at Atyrau Railway Station Renovation
item.description: A worker fell five meters during the renovation of Atyrau railway station and is now in a coma. The man's condition is critical, with doctors using special medications to stabilize his circulation. A criminal case has been initiated regarding violations of labor protection requirements. The renovation, which began in March 2026, has faced previous safety concerns.

item.title: SCO-Afghanistan Contact Group Activities Paused, Deputy Secretary-General States
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)-Afghanistan Contact Group's activities have been paused, according to SCO Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Saidmuradov. While the situation in Afghanistan remains controlled, risks of sharp deterioration persist. He stated this at a conference in Moscow focused on security in Central Asia and Afghanistan.

item.title: Taliban and Pakistan Forces Exchange Fire in Paktia Province Border Area
item.description: Clashes have erupted between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces in the Dand Patan district of Paktia province, with Pakistan reportedly firing artillery shells. Local sources indicate civilians are trapped and some families have fled their homes due to indiscriminate shelling. The Taliban are conducting defensive attacks in response. Reasons for the clashes and casualties remain unclear.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Imprisoned for Life in South Korea Released After 16 Years
item.description: Akmal Bozorov, an Uzbek citizen sentenced to life imprisonment in South Korea for the murder of a taxi driver at age 19, has been released after 16 years. The court decided to halt the execution of the sentence due to the use of brutality and illegal methods during the investigation, ordering a review of the case.

item.title: Taliban Discuss Afghanistan Railway Projects at ECO Meeting in Astana
item.description: The Taliban discussed Afghanistan railway projects, including routes to Turkmenistan and Iran, at the 14th ECO meeting in Astana. The head of the Taliban Railway Authority met with representatives from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, and Iran to discuss joint railway initiatives and the launch of passenger train services between Afghanistan and Iran.

item.title: Taliban Declare 24.4 Hectares in Kabul's Paghman District State-Owned
item.description: The Taliban have declared approximately 24.4 hectares of land in Kabul's Paghman district as "state-owned" following a ruling by a special court. The Ministry of Justice stated the land in Arghandi Sufla was declared state property after reviewing documents. This declaration follows previous claims of land usurpation by the Taliban.

item.title: New 1600 MW Sirdaryo-2 power plant to strengthen Uzbekistan's energy system this winter
item.description: The 1600 MW Sirdaryo-2 combined cycle power plant will begin strengthening Uzbekistan's energy system this winter. EDF's executive vice president announced the nearing completion of the plant during a meeting with energy sector investors. Construction of the Surxondaryo plant is 75% complete, and a wind farm project is also underway.

item.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang lays wreath at Independence Monument in Uzbekistan
item.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang, on an official visit to Uzbekistan, laid a wreath at the Independence Monument in the "New Uzbekistan" park. He was accompanied by Uzbek Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov. Li Qiang was briefed on the monument's concept, reflecting Uzbekistan's history and people.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Access to Innovative Health Monitoring Features on Smartwatches
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has expanded access to innovative health monitoring features on Apple Watch, Samsung Galaxy Watch, and AirPods Pro. Direct agreements with manufacturers allow users to record ECGs, measure blood pressure, and receive alerts for irregular heart rhythms and sleep apnea risks. New medical services will be available to Kazakh users simultaneously with their global launch.

item.title: Samarkand Declaration Marks New Phase in Human Rights Protection and International Cooperation
item.description: The Samarkand Declaration signifies a new stage in protecting human rights and fostering international cooperation. Samarkand is emerging as a global political center and diplomatic hub, hosting major summits. The VII Congress of the Association of Asian Constitutional Courts in Samarkand focused on future priorities and strengthening collaboration among members.

item.title: Poverty and Unemployment Drive Young Afghans to Risk Dangerous Migration
item.description: Experts attribute the continued migration of young Afghans to a lack of job opportunities, economic hardship, and a bleak future outlook. Many leave out of necessity, seeking security, employment, and education. Migration expert Asefa Stanikzai warns that addressing root causes like insecurity and lack of opportunity is crucial to reduce forced migration.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Exports Surge to $60.4 Billion, Driven by Agricultural Products
item.description: Kazakhstan's foreign trade turnover reached $103 billion in January-August 2026, a 12.8% increase year-on-year. Exports grew by 19.5% to $60.4 billion, significantly outpacing import growth. Key drivers included a 48.5% rise in sunflower oil exports and a 26.5% increase in wheat exports.

item.title: President's Relative Nurassyl Medeu to Transfer One of Two Educational Institutions to State
item.description: Nurassyl Medeu, a relative of the President, announced he will transfer one of two educational institutions mentioned in an Azattyq investigation to the state. The Kazakh National University of Sports will be "voluntarily transferred" without sale or management transfer, ensuring all student obligations and founder grants are met.

item.title: Astana Hosts Meeting of Ministers of Information of Turkic States Organization
item.description: Astana hosted the 8th meeting of ministers and high-ranking officials responsible for information from member states of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS). Discussions focused on the impact of modern technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, on the media landscape and emerging challenges in the information space.

item.title: India Plans to Sell Seized Tanker with Kazakh National Onboard
item.description: India intends to sell the seized tanker Unity, which has been under arrest since May 11, 2026, near the port of Paradip. A relative of a crew member expressed concern that sailors might be left on the vessel until its sale. The tanker, flying the flag of Cameroon, is involved in a financial dispute. Kazakh diplomats are working on repatriation.

item.title: Afghanistan Railways Chief Attends ECO Regional Meeting in Kazakhstan
item.description: Abdul Karim Fateh, head of the Afghanistan Railway Authority, attended the 14th Regional Meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in Astana, Kazakhstan. The meeting focused on new railway projects. The spokesperson for the Ministry of Public Works of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan confirmed Fateh's participation and the meeting's agenda.

item.title: UN Secretary-General Guterres: Poverty is an Insult to Human Dignity and Must Be Eradicated
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that poverty is an "insult" to human dignity and a denial of human rights, emphasizing the need for its eradication through political will and investment. He highlighted that the resources and knowledge exist globally to end poverty, but collective action is required to address inequalities and ensure everyone can live with dignity.

item.title: India Plans to Sell Seized Tanker with Kazakh National Aboard
item.description: An arrested tanker, the Unity, carrying a Kazakh national, is slated for sale in India. Sailors fear being stranded until a new crew arrives. The tanker has been under arrest since May 11, 2026, near the Indian port of Paradip due to a financial dispute. Kazakh diplomats are working on the repatriation of their citizen.

item.title: Taliban Accused of Excavating Hesar Archaeological Site and Removing Historical Artifacts
item.description: The Panjshir Studies Centre reports the Taliban excavated the Hesar archaeological site in Panjshir Province, unearthing and removing historical artifacts. The center expressed concern over the artifacts' fate and urged an end to destructive activities. They called on UNESCO to investigate the damage and urged the Taliban to protect cultural heritage.

item.title: Kazakh Ministry Explains Varying State Support for Families with Equal Number of Children
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection is clarifying new approaches to state support, effective January 1, 2027. The ministry explained that families with the same number of children may require different levels of support based on their actual living circumstances, not just categorical status. This aims to provide aid based on real needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Scientific Cooperation with Tatarstan and UN Investment Dispute Reform
item.description: Kazakhstan participated in international events in Kazan and Vienna, focusing on scientific, economic, and cultural cooperation, as well as new rules for resolving investor-state disputes. In Kazan, a roundtable marked Kazakhstan's 35 years of independence, fostering collaboration with Tatarstan in industry, science, and culture. Vienna session addressed reforms in international investment arbitration.

item.title: Premier of China's State Council Li Qiang Arrives in Uzbekistan
item.description: Li Qiang, Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, has arrived in Uzbekistan for a two-day official visit. He was welcomed at Tashkent International Airport by Uzbek Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov and other officials. The visit includes high-level talks, signing of bilateral documents, and exploring Uzbekistan's cultural heritage.
